title: Clinical Benefit of Hinged Elbow Bracing in the Postoperative Treatment of Complex Elbow Fracture-Dislocations A Matched-Pair Analysis
summary: Following surgery for a severe elbow injury (where the joint is both dislocated and fractured), the arm is currently protected as standard practice with a special hinged brace for six weeks. However, because this brace often slips in everyday life and its actual benefit remains unclear, this study at the BG Unfallklinik Frankfurt am Main investigates whether healing progresses just as well and safely without a brace. To test this, newly operated adult patients perform their regular, non-weight-bearing movement exercises for six weeks without wearing a brace. Over the course of one year, mobility, pain, and potential complications are recorded during routine follow-up appointments and compared with the outcomes of previous patients who wore a brace. The goal is to determine whether the brace can be omitted in the future to simplify postoperative care.
